reviewNotes.sections.religion: Drafted as 'religion and community'; some families write धर्म एवं जाति.
reviewNotes.sections.career: Drafted as व्यवसाय विवरण; नौकरी / व्यवसाय is also common.
reviewNotes.sections.contact: संपर्क सूत्र, as printed on many Hindi biodatas.
reviewNotes.sections.references: Drafted as संदर्भ (people who vouch for the family); परिचित is an alternative.
reviewNotes.fields.height: कद, the everyday word on biodatas; ऊँचाई is the formal one.
reviewNotes.fields.nakshatraPada: Printed as चरण, the usual Hindi word for a nakshatra's pada.
reviewNotes.fields.maternalGotra: Drafted as मामा का गोत्र; ननिहाल का गोत्र is also used.
reviewNotes.fields.college: Borrowed कॉलेज, as families write it; महाविद्यालय is the formal word.
reviewNotes.fields.employer: Borrowed कंपनी; संस्थान fits government and other employers better.
reviewNotes.fields.kulaDevata: कुलदेवता; many families write कुलदेवी instead.
reviewNotes.fields.muslimSect: Generic संप्रदाय; मसलक or फ़िरक़ा may read more naturally to Muslim families.
reviewNotes.fields.denomination: Generic संप्रदाय for a Christian denomination.
reviewNotes.options.maritalStatus.widowed: Gendered pair विधुर / विधवा printed together; no neutral everyday word.
reviewNotes.options.familyValues.liberal: Drafted as आधुनिक ('modern'); उदार is the literal word.
reviewNotes.options.motherTongue.bengali: बंगाली, the everyday Hindi form; बांग्ला is the language's own name.
reviewNotes.relations.brotherInLaw: जीजा is the sister's husband; साला / देवर are other brothers-in-law.
reviewNotes.relations.sisterInLaw: भाभी is the brother's wife; साली / ननद are other sisters-in-law.
reviewNotes.relations.grandfather: दादा is paternal; नाना is maternal. Some families add जी to every relation.
reviewNotes.relations.grandmother: दादी is paternal; नानी is maternal.
reviewNotes.relations.paternalUncle: चाचा is the father's younger brother; ताऊ the elder.
reviewNotes.relations.uncle: Hindi has no neutral word for uncle; borrowed अंकल. A reviewer may prefer फूफा / मौसा.
reviewNotes.relations.aunt: Borrowed आंटी, for the same reason; चाची / मामी / फूफी are specific.
reviewNotes.relations.cousin: Borrowed कज़िन; चचेरा / ममेरा / फुफेरा / मौसेरा भाई or बहन are specific.
reviewNotes.titles.marriageBiodata: विवाह बायोडाटा; विवाह परिचय पत्र is a more formal alternative.
reviewNotes.words.am: Kept as AM/PM, common on printed biodatas; प्रातः / सायं is an alternative.
reviewNotes.fields.intiPeru: Step 2.0 (Telugu chip): the family name a Telugu biodata prints before the given name (ఇంటి పేరు); drafted as the usual word for 'surname'.
reviewNotes.fields.devak: Step 2.0 (Marathi chip): the family's devak (clan totem); transliterated.
reviewNotes.fields.gan: Step 2.0: gana used in guna matching (Deva / Manushya / Rakshasa).
reviewNotes.fields.maslak: Step 2.0 (Muslim chip): school or jamaat (Hanafi, Deobandi, Barelvi…); transliterated.
reviewNotes.titles.bioData: Step 2.0: the hyphenated 'Bio-Data' spelling many printed biodatas use.
